description:
Found by an s423 (#418) review probe, and PRE-EXISTING for ASCII names too â
the non-ASCII case behaves exactly like the ASCII one, which is why it did not
block #418 (same shape as #430).

    package Foo;
    sub AUTOLOAD { our $AUTOLOAD; my $n = $AUTOLOAD; $n =~ s/.*:://; return "auto:$n" }
    sub DESTROY {}
    package main;
    print Foo->anything, "\n";     # perl: auto:anything   PCL: auto:anything  (OK)
    print Foo::other(), "\n";      # perl: auto:other      PCL: CRASH

PCL: "The function Foo::pl-other is undefined" â an undefined-function error
out of the emitted `(Foo::pl-other)` call, with an empty line printed first.
The METHOD form works (p-method-call falls back to AUTOLOAD); the plain
package-qualified CALL is emitted as a direct CL function call, so there is no
dispatch point at which AUTOLOAD could be consulted.

perl looks for &Foo::other, fails, then walks the same package (and, for a
method call, the MRO) for AUTOLOAD, sets $AUTOLOAD to the FULL name
"Foo::other" and calls it.

Fix shape (design question the task carries): the emitted call would have to
go through a resolver that can miss â either emit `(p-call-sub "Foo::other" â¦)`
for a name PCL cannot see a definition for at compile time (a cost on every
such call), or install an AUTOLOAD trampoline as the function binding when a
package defines AUTOLOAD (cheap, but needs the definition to be visible when
the call is READ).  Measure which spelling the corpus actually uses before
choosing; the utf8 twin (probes q07/q07a of s423) is the same bug.

Reproducer: the six-line program above, plus its fullwidth twin
(package ï¼¦ï¼¯ï¼¯, ï¼¦ï¼¯ï¼¯::other()) â identical behaviour, which is the evidence
that #418 did not cause it.
title: AUTOLOAD is not consulted for a plain qualified sub call (Foo::other())
